html:
The founding of the Empire of Nicaea in western Anatolia after the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople in 1204. It was the largest of the Greek successor states and lasted until it won back Constantinople in 1261.

Theodore Laskaris gathered the Greek cities of western Anatolia and was crowned emperor at Nicaea, where the Orthodox patriarch also settled. The state held off both the Latin Empire in Constantinople and the Seljuks.

Under John III Vatatzes (1221 to 1254) Nicaea grew rich and strong, encouraged farming and self sufficiency, and spread into the Balkans, beating its Greek rival in Epirus. In 1259 Michael VIII Palaiologos seized power. In 1261 his general found Constantinople weakly guarded and walked in, and the empire was restored in its old capital. Nicaea's rival in the east, the Empire of Trebizond, stayed independent.
